nodes.name: Drop SPF from planning
nodes.prompt:

Read context/architecture.md, context/fix-plan-2026-11-17.md (stream A) and the current QuestSharing/QuestPlanner.lua buildRoute/planOptions/solve/refine and QuestOptimizer.lua place() first. You own ONLY: QuestSharing/QuestPlanner.lua, QuestSharing/QuestOptimizer.lua, QuestSharing/QuestPlannerPath.lua, tests/test_quest_planner_zone_steps.py, tests/test_quest_optimizer.py, tests/test_quest_planner_path.py, CHANGELOG.md, README.md. Do NOT edit QuestSharing/DataWork.lua or tests/test_data_budget.py (stream D2 owns them).
Do: (1) Planning uses only straight-line travel: remove every Path.estimateWalks / Path.cancelWalkEstimates / Path.prioritizeFirstOuting use from QuestPlanner.lua, the firstLeg walking table, the walking/walkCosted/shown flags, opts.lockSites and the 'quest-costs' job; delete estimateWalks, cancelWalkEstimates and prioritizeFirstOuting from QuestPlannerPath.lua (keep Path.available and Path.follow — the optional Follow arrow stays). Remove lockSites support from QuestOptimizer.place(). (2) Keep camp stickiness without SPF: record siteMemory from every solve and pass preferredSites with the existing 25%/20 s margin, BUT never record a site for a stop whose camps were narrowed or promoted by avoidBusyCamps (keep the memory from before the busy mark), and reset siteMemory in the 'Clear camp wait' handler. (3) Start the background refinement as an idle-priority job using this contract owned by stream D2: Work.start(owner, run, valid, finished, budget, priority) where priority == 'idle' runs only when no non-idle job is runnable; call Work.start('quest-improve', run, valid, nil, nil, 'idle'). (Until D2 lands the extra argument is simply ignored.) (4) Keep A1 (selection survives the swap), A3 (mixed camps), A4 (yield every 32 actions, refine-only-on-input-change gate, busy keys in inputs) and A5 behaviour. (5) Tests, failing-first where behaviour changes: rewrite the SPF-specific tests so that with SPF installed (v1, v2.2, v2.3 mocks, delivering or failing estimates) the planner never calls EstimateWalks and the camp timeline/route equal the no-SPF plan (switch at POS 0.56); busy -> alternative camp, 'Clear camp wait' -> original camp, wait expiry + small move -> original camp; the Follow button test in test_quest_planner_path.py still passes. (6) Docs: in CHANGELOG.md '## Unreleased' replace the bullet that starts 'Quest guide with Shortest Path Forever' with: the quest guide no longer uses Shortest Path Forever walking estimates to choose camps or order steps (SPF is only used for the optional Follow arrow), so the guide behaves the same with or without it; add: the background route refinement now runs only when no other data work is waiting, so map search and the dungeon scan keep full speed while the guide is open. Also add stream D3's map-number bullet only if the final check asks; do not touch QuestGuidance.lua. Fix README.md lines that describe SPF walking costs in planning, and update the stale test counts (README says test_vendor_map has 88 tests -> use the real current count; test_quest_planner_zone_steps 28 -> real count). In CHANGELOG.md reword the C1 dungeon bullet's last sentence to 'Menus opened from other Quest Sharing windows are no longer closed when the quest log updates.' (the scan-completion and open refreshes still close menus). Run from tests/ with /tmp/qs-test-env/bin/python: test_quest_optimizer, test_quest_planner_zone_steps, test_quest_planner_path, test_quest_planner_guide, test_quest_planner_ui, test_quest_guidance, test_planner_facts, test_data_budget (run, do not edit); compile both Lua files under lupa.lua51. nodes.name: Add idle job priority
nodes.prompt:
Repo /Users/cozzolif/Desktop/cutpdf (WoW addon, Lua 5.1). Read context/architecture.md and QuestSharing/DataWork.lua first. Problem: DataWork gives every queued job one resume per turn regardless of cost, so the quest guide's background route refinement ('quest-improve') slows map search ('vendor-index'/'vendor-search') to about 10% and the dungeon scan to about 80% of their solo pace. You own ONLY: QuestSharing/DataWork.lua, tests/test_data_budget.py, QuestSharing/VendorMap.lua (retry fix only), tests/test_vendor_map.py, QuestSharing/Menu.lua and QuestSharing/DungeonQuests.lua (accessor only), tests/test_dungeon_quests.py, tests/test_menu.py. Do NOT edit QuestPlanner.lua or QuestOptimizer.lua (stream D1 calls your API).
Do: (1) Contract: W.start(owner, run, valid, finished, budget, priority). priority == 'idle' means the job is resumed in a pump only when no non-idle job is runnable (queued, not paused, valid). Idle jobs keep their order, still obey the 2 ms / 80-step slice, pause in combat, cancel/pause/resume/busy work as before; default (nil) priority keeps today's behaviour exactly. (2) Tests first in tests/test_data_budget.py: a synthetic idle job that loops forever next to a normal job: the normal job keeps >= 90% of its solo pumps; the idle job still finishes when alone; an idle job started before a normal job yields to it; existing budget tests (including the 2.8 ms share test and no-preload tests) still pass. (3) Small leftover from the map-search review: after an internal vendor job failure, an explicit search with the same text (Enter, search icon, Ctrl+right-click) must retry (VendorMap.lua ~:714 V.search / ~:791 'failed == generation'); add a test in tests/test_vendor_map.py. (4) Small leftover from the dungeon review: add a public accessor ns.questMenuEntry() in QuestSharing/Menu.lua returning the open quest menu's entry (or nil), keep ns._questMenu for tests, and make QuestSharing/DungeonQuests.lua use ns.questMenuEntry() instead of ns._questMenu(); test_dungeon_quests.py and test_menu.py must pass. Return a one-line CHANGELOG suggestion in your summary (stream D1 owns CHANGELOG). Run from tests/ with /tmp/qs-test-env/bin/python: test_data_budget, test_vendor_map, test_dungeon_quests, test_menu, test_quest_optimizer (run, do not edit); compile changed Lua under lupa.lua51. Report files, summary and test results.

nodes.name: Raise map step numbers
nodes.prompt: Repo /Users/cozzolif/Desktop/cutpdf (WoW addon, Lua 5.1). User report: the quest-guide step numbers drawn on the world map are hard to read and sometimes render UNDER the map; they must always stay on top and be clearly visible. Read context/architecture.md, context/BUGS/2026-11-17-guidance-selected-cluster-marker.md and QuestSharing/QuestGuidance.lua (makeMarker ~:100-121, drawMap ~:162-243) first. You own ONLY QuestSharing/QuestGuidance.lua and tests/test_quest_guidance.py (return a CHANGELOG snippet instead of editing CHANGELOG). Root cause found by the orchestrator: (a) the overlay 'QuestSharingRouteOverlay' is parented to WorldMapFrame.ScrollContainer.Child at frame level child+10, set only when the canvas changes, so native/addon map pins (pin frame levels far above +10) and later map level changes draw over it; (b) markers use GameFontHighlightSmall with no outline, white on a dark teal face with a 1 px border. Do, failing tests first: (1) on EVERY drawMap re-apply the overlay level: min(9900, childLevel + 2000), markers at overlay+2 (active +3), legend at overlay+1, keep the same strata as the canvas; also re-apply when the map is shown. (3) Tests in tests/test_quest_guidance.py: a mock native pin frame on the canvas at child+500 stays below every marker; after the canvas raises its own level by 300 and the map redraws, markers are still above it; marker font flags contain OUTLINE and size >= 13; selected marker border is gold; all existing guidance tests (zoom constant size, grouping, click/cycle, combat hide, submap) still pass. Report files, summary, tests and a CHANGELOG '## Unreleased' snippet.
